forest_07_001.speaker: narrator
forest_07_001.text: The western patch sounded different with a working crew in it. Shovels struck stones; saws rasped; someone dropped a tin cup and accused the hillside of theft. Shi Lan moved between the marked edges while the senior fireline worker assigned the first lengths. Lin received a short section on stable ground with a partner who had done this before. He showed her how to cut beneath the litter without flinging it into the cleared strip behind them. Her first attempt did precisely that.

forest_07_002.speaker: narrator
forest_07_002.text: Her partner let her look at the scattered debris, then handed her the shovel again. The second attempt was better and much slower. He said slower was normal until her hands learned the angle. Wen passed along the level supply path carrying replacement handles and lunch water, his knee now cleared for that route. He saw Lin's concentration and wisely did not ask whether cultivation made shoveling effortless. Her face already contained an answer.

forest_07_003.speaker: lin_yue
forest_07_003.text: The ground is behaving like an examiner who has never heard of my sect. I would like to impress it, but every time I swing harder, I throw the wrong thing into the wrong place. Your method is less dramatic and works. I will use it. If I begin looking dramatic again, please point to the strip behind me. I can endure the embarrassment. I cannot endure having to clear the same three paces for a fourth time.

forest_07_004.speaker: narrator
forest_07_004.text: By midday, her section exposed firm mineral soil between two marked pins. The senior worker inspected its width and the uphill litter edge. He found a thin root bridge Lin had missed and asked her to clear around it without damaging the larger living root beneath. She had mistaken a clean surface for a completed line. The distinction was tiring. So was the root. She knelt, worked carefully, and stood with a stiff back that no one praised as spiritually meaningful.

forest_07_005.speaker: narrator
forest_07_005.text: At lunch, the crew sat on dry sacks outside the work edge. One man had brought a boiled egg wrapped in a page of old arithmetic. He complained that his son now learned sums with better paper than he had ever owned. Another worker asked whether the egg could solve the shortage. Wen said it could solve one person's lunch. The man ate it before anyone assigned it a public duty. Lin found herself laughing with a mouth full of beans.

forest_07_006.speaker: narrator
forest_07_006.text: Shi Lan ate standing until the senior worker pointed at the empty sack beside him. She sat. He asked whether her left wrist still ached in cold weather. She flexed it once and said sometimes. The burn scar lay mostly beneath her sleeve, but Lin saw a pale edge when she reached for the kettle. Wen looked away politely. The warden noticed that too and said they could all stop treating a wrist as a tragic guest at lunch.

forest_07_007.speaker: shi_lan
forest_07_007.text: It is an old scar. It does not predict today's fire. The mistake that made it is more useful to remember than the scar itself. I went back into a smoldering edge to retrieve a tool after we thought the ground was cold. The tool was not worth my hand. The man who came after me was hurt worse. You may ask about the procedure we changed. Please do not ask whether I became wiser at the exact moment it blistered. Mostly I swore.

forest_07_008.speaker: narrator
forest_07_008.text: The senior worker nodded at the last sentence with evident authority. Lin asked how they checked cold ground now. He described the qualified crew's layered inspection and later rechecks, including probing places where concealed heat could persist. She would assist with recording only if assigned; handling a shovel did not qualify her to clear an extinguished patch. The explanation was practical and brief. Shi Lan seemed relieved when Wen asked whether the swearing procedure had also been standardized.

forest_07_009.speaker: narrator
forest_07_009.text: The afternoon crew moved to the manual-removal strip near the deep soil seam. Cut debris was carried to the approved disposal stack, not piled over the wet hollow or the animal passage. The stack had room for the planned quantity. When one worker began a second pile beside the path to save distance, the senior worker redirected him before it grew. The man grumbled but moved it. Nobody wrote a treatise about the grumble. They had enough branches to carry.

forest_07_010.speaker: narrator
forest_07_010.text: Lin's gloves wore thin at the thumb. She noticed only when a splinter found the gap. Her partner stopped with her, helped remove the splinter from the superficial skin, and pointed her toward the wash station and spare-glove box. The box contained three sizes, none exactly hers. She chose the least awkward pair. Wen inspected the old glove and said it had worked hard for a garment with no ambition. She told him the garment was considering a quieter profession.

forest_07_011.speaker: narrator
forest_07_011.text: On the upper edge, the qualified saw crew began assessing the dead firs. The first trunk had a hollow so broad that a man could put his hand into it. The crew chose a drop direction away from the refuge and cleared people well beyond the marked reach. Lin watched from the safe assembly point. The tree fell with a tearing sound that she felt in her teeth. Inside its broken base lay a dark chamber full of damp, crumbling wood.

forest_07_012.speaker: narrator
forest_07_012.text: The usable portions were measured for their authorized disposition; rotten material went to the planned debris handling. Long's manager had come expecting bonus fuel. He saw the hollow trunk and stopped suggesting quantities. The saw leader explained why the remaining leaning trees would take longer than a straight count implied. The manager asked whether he could take that explanation to Long. Shi Lan said yes. He asked the leader to show him the dangerous branch again, from the safe place.

forest_07_013.speaker: narrator
forest_07_013.text: A thin sun reached the work strip in late afternoon. Snow melted from the exposed soil and ran beneath the litter at the shaded edge. Shi Lan changed the next day's digging order so the wet section would be assessed before people widened it blindly. The crew had made visible progress. It had not made every marked pace equally suitable. Lin looked back along her short completed section and felt proud enough to resent the next pin waiting farther uphill.

forest_07_014.speaker: wen_cai
forest_07_014.text: You are glaring at the pin. I recognize the expression. It is the one my uncle gives a sack when he believes it should have become lighter out of respect. The pin has no feelings. We can stop for today without insulting it. Come back tomorrow and glare from the other side after you have done the next length. That will teach it. I have no evidence for this method, but I am willing to call it a family tradition.

forest_07_015.speaker: narrator
forest_07_015.text: At the end-of-shift count, one worker asked for another hour to finish his section. The senior worker refused because his partner had already left and the late work had not been authorized or rostered. The man said he needed the extra wage. Shi Lan asked him to speak at the office about available paid shifts rather than invent one on a hazardous line. His disappointment was sharp. Lin watched him shoulder his empty lunch bag and leave without pretending the answer had fed him.

forest_07_016.speaker: narrator
forest_07_016.text: The worker returned to the office that evening. His household had received a reduced winter hiring turn elsewhere, and he was trying to make up the loss. The available fireline shifts were finite. Pei referred him to two ordinary tasks funded for the following week and the hardship desk for immediate food need. He accepted the tasks and declined relief. Pei did not argue in front of the room. Lin later found him counting coins beneath the porch lantern.

forest_07_017.speaker: narrator
forest_07_017.text: She nearly offered her own money before remembering the bowls Wen's sister had actually wanted. Instead, she asked whether he wanted help reading the posted work times. He said he could read. The sharpness embarrassed them both. Lin said she had assumed too much and began to leave. He called her back to ask whether the lower maintenance task required boots with a sound sole. His heel had split. She directed him to the work-equipment allowance stated on the notice.

forest_07_018.speaker: narrator
forest_07_018.text: The allowance provided a modest repair, not new boots for everyone. The worker brought his pair to the named cobbler and agreed on the funded mend. Lin did not follow him inside. She had already come too close to treating his difficulty as her lesson. At the lodging, she washed the small splinter wound and stretched her sore fingers. The day had improved the fireline by a few measured lengths. It had made her less graceful in several conversations.

forest_07_019.speaker: narrator
forest_07_019.text: Wen's sister was sleeping when Lin arrived for the agreed washing turn. The intended husband had done most of the bowls already and asked her to finish quietly. Through the partly open door she could see the new roof beam above the bedding. Its ordinary shadow looked secure. She washed the last three bowls and left without waking anyone. On the path home, the patched glove in her pocket rubbed against the sealed edge of her mother's outgoing letter receipt.

forest_07_020.speaker: narrator
forest_07_020.text: At the watch station, no Harts had approached the bridge that day. Tracks showed both animals moving through the protected upper turn. The watchman said the younger one seemed to be placing the leg more evenly, then added that the snow was firmer too. Lin smiled at the careful qualification. She had heard enough careless certainty to value a man who let his hopeful observation remain small. Beyond him, the hollow held its cold as though storing it for later.

forest_07_021.speaker: narrator
forest_07_021.text: Shi Lan was still awake when Lin reached the lodging. The warden had spread tomorrow's roster across the table, leaving space for the senior worker's adjustments. The niece slept with the paper dog's tether looped around one finger. Lin sat down to mend her glove. Shi Lan watched the clumsy stitches and offered no advice until asked. Outside, the forest waited beneath a clear, bitter sky. Inside, two women worked at things that would be slightly more usable in the morning.

forest_07_022.speaker: narrator
forest_07_022.text: On the second preparation day, the senior worker found his kettle frozen solid. He held it up accusingly, as if winter had violated a personal agreement. Shi Lan lent him her small flask. Wen asked whether the kettle had become an approved ice reservoir. The worker said it had become evidence that young men should speak less before tea. Lin carried the first pin bundle up the path, grateful that her section required more walking than conversation while her shoulders loosened.

forest_07_023.speaker: narrator
forest_07_023.text: The wet edge had worsened overnight. Water beneath the litter froze unevenly, hiding soft patches beside firm ones. The deputy closed a short section for closer assessment and shifted the crew to stable ground. Long's manager asked how the delay affected the proposed ignition window. Shi Lan said there was no approved window yet. He had brought a town letter referring to one. She took the letter and found a tentative planning date described as scheduled work.

forest_07_024.speaker: shi_lan
forest_07_024.text: Who changed tentative to scheduled? I will answer the timetable after I know which timetable people have been given. We discussed a possible week, conditional on preparation and weather. If your customers now believe a fire will happen that week, they have been told something this crew has not agreed. I want the corrected notice sent today. Do not make me discover it later while somebody accuses the rain of breaking a contract it never read.

forest_07_025.speaker: narrator
forest_07_025.text: The manager said Long's office had shortened the planning note for a customer circular. He admitted he had written the circular himself. Long was called to the patch in the afternoon. He inspected the wet edge, read the original note, and authorized the correction without defending its usefulness. Then he asked Shi Lan whether she could give the office an earlier warning if the likely week slipped. She said she could report observations. She could not forecast away the conditional ground.

forest_07_026.speaker: long_qian
forest_07_026.text: My customers want a date because they arrange their own work around deliveries. I keep trying to give them certainty by shaving off the words that make a date honest. It is an expensive habit. Send the correction. I will also tell the office to copy the condition beside the date, not at the end of another page. If the letter becomes longer, buy more paper. I would rather pay the printer than pay for what a short sentence makes somebody attempt.

forest_07_027.speaker: narrator
forest_07_027.text: The senior worker listened, then asked Long to help carry a short stack of cut branches to the approved pile. Long hesitated and accepted. He had excellent boots and poor gloves for the task. By the third load his cuffs were full of needles. Nobody laughed until he tried to shake them out and put half of them into his collar. Then everyone laughed, including him. His manager fetched better gloves from the spare box with impressive speed.

forest_07_028.speaker: narrator
forest_07_028.text: Wen returned from a water turn to find Long hauling branches. He stared openly. Long asked whether a grain buyer was physically forbidden to lift wood. Wen said no, but they might have to notify the licensing office about such a rare event. Shi Lan told both men to keep the stack below its marked height. Long put his final branch down carefully. The stack did not care whether labor had been performed sincerely, strategically, or with a collar full of fir needles.

forest_07_029.speaker: narrator
forest_07_029.text: At the shaded seam, the deputy's probe found a buried old root mass extending farther than the first inspection suggested. The proposed burn edge had to move again. Manual removal would cover the added strip. That meant more labor before ignition and less convenient ground for the fireline. The senior worker redrew the work estimate on his board. His thumb rubbed away an old figure reluctantly. He had hoped to finish before the coming weather changed.

forest_07_030.speaker: narrator
forest_07_030.text: Shi Lan reviewed the additional hours with the council, using the preparation allowance's remaining margin and deferring a lower-priority fence painting task. The fence would remain sound and unpainted through the interval. The clerk complained that the painting had already been promised to two workers. They were offered the added debris shifts if suited and willing, with their original accepted hiring terms honored where necessary. One took the replacement. The other had a bad shoulder and needed a different level task.

forest_07_031.speaker: narrator
forest_07_031.text: The man with the bad shoulder ended up mending gathering baskets at the shelter. Lin watched him weave a broken rim so neatly that the repaired side looked stronger than the original. He said the ridge had enough people willing to drag things uphill and too few people willing to notice what could be mended downhill. She brought him the damaged basket from the Hart incident after its owner agreed to the quoted repair. He inspected it and pronounced the beast a poor craftsman.

forest_07_032.speaker: narrator
forest_07_032.text: By the fourth workday, Lin could clear a short line section without repeatedly scattering debris behind her. Her partner began leaving her to finish the easier lengths while he worked around the root bridges. She felt trusted and immediately wanted to justify it by moving faster. A crooked cut caught her shovel. She stopped, reset, and resumed the learned angle. The trust survived an ordinary pause. That seemed worth remembering without writing it on another page.

forest_07_033.speaker: narrator
forest_07_033.text: Wen carried water and spare handles along the level path. His knee held under the staged return. He checked it at each rest, sometimes so ostentatiously that the senior worker accused him of courting it. Wen replied that the knee had been difficult but influential. Lin nearly dropped her cup laughing. Shi Lan asked whether they could all finish lunch without giving human joints a place in the commission hierarchy. The worker said his back already occupied the senior position.

forest_07_034.speaker: narrator
forest_07_034.text: The worker whose boots had been repaired arrived late and pale on the fifth morning. He said he had slept badly. The senior worker put him on a lighter task near the shelter and told him to report if the dizziness continued. He insisted he was fit. Lin noticed his hands tremble while he tied a branch bundle. She told the worker supervising that task, who shortened his load and sent him for water. The man looked humiliated by the attention.

forest_07_035.speaker: narrator
forest_07_035.text: Before the next rest, he tried to lift a heavier bundle alone. His shoulder jerked, and he dropped it with a cry. The branches fell inside the designated stack area, missing the nearest worker. The senior worker stopped the task. The man sat on the ground, furious at himself, and said it was only a pull. Shi Lan called the clinic assistant. Lin fetched the stool instead of helping him demonstrate that he could still stand proudly under a load.

forest_07_036.speaker: narrator
forest_07_036.text: The clinic assistant found pain and restricted shoulder movement without an obvious dislocation. She advised rest from lifting and a later examination if the pain worsened. The man admitted he had worked an additional late sorting shift at a different yard, then walked home after midnight. He had needed the wage. He had not told the morning supervisor how little he slept because he feared being sent away without pay. The supervisor looked at Shi Lan. Their roster had not caused his other shift, but it had met its tired body.

forest_07_037.speaker: shi_lan
forest_07_037.text: Today's completed hours will be paid. The rest of the scheduled shift goes under the injury and medical review terms, not under a punishment for telling us late. We need your account of the extra work and the lift. We also need to explain our rest requirement better before the next roster. I cannot make every household expense disappear. I can stop pretending that a man becomes rested because one office writes a tidy daytime schedule.

forest_07_038.speaker: narrator
forest_07_038.text: The man cried once, sharply, and looked away. Nobody spoke for a moment. Then the basket mender, who had come to deliver repaired rims, asked whether he wanted company to the clinic. He accepted. The pair left slowly, discussing the quality of the repaired boots as though the shoulder were a stranger following them. Lin watched them go and felt how close concern could stand to shame. Her partner gave her an ordinary small bundle, bringing her back to the work still safe to do.

forest_07_039.speaker: narrator
forest_07_039.text: The remaining crew shortened the afternoon task rather than absorb the injured man's load at a frantic pace. The senior worker revised the completion estimate again. Long's manager was present and wrote the change without asking for a shortcut. Shi Lan looked tired enough that Lin wanted to tell her the response had been good. Instead, she asked whether the warden had eaten. Shi Lan stared at her, then laughed with an edge of surrender. The niece had evidently trained more than one inspector.

forest_07_040.speaker: narrator
forest_07_040.text: That evening the council reviewed the shoulder injury and the competing work shifts. The man's immediate food application was still open because he had declined relief earlier; he now asked to reconsider it. The ordinary criteria allowed the review without requiring him to praise the scheme. His family received a bounded portion through the existing allotment. The basket mender took him home. Pei asked Lin to leave the injury papers in the office and go wash the dirt from her own hands.

forest_07_041.speaker: narrator
forest_07_041.text: At the lodging, Wen was teaching the niece a new paper creature with wings. She called it a flying kettle, which offended the senior worker when he came to collect his actual kettle. He had thawed it safely and wanted it back before anyone appointed it a monster. Lin sat on the floor to help crease the wings. Her shovel hands made delicate folding difficult. The child told her to slow down, with the complete confidence of a teacher who had never cleared a fireline.

forest_07_042.speaker: narrator
forest_07_042.text: Lin slowed down. The paper wings opened evenly on the second attempt. Shi Lan watched from the table, her own roster unfinished. For a while, nobody asked her about the possible burn week. The child flew the kettle across the room and landed it on the marked map, exactly inside the deep-soil exclusion. Wen declared it a wise kettle. Shi Lan removed it gently before its wings smudged the pencil. Tomorrow the crew would finish the revised line if the ground allowed.

forest_07_043.speaker: narrator
forest_07_043.text: The next morning, a red flag was missing from the western line. Its pin still stood, with a short piece of severed string clinging to it. The senior worker stopped preparation along that edge until Shi Lan checked the markings. The flag might have been taken by wind, a careless passerby, or a deliberate hand. The clean end of the string favored cutting, but it did not name the cutter. Wen found the flag folded beneath a nearby stump.

forest_07_044.speaker: narrator
forest_07_044.text: Inside the fold lay a note: do not burn here. No signature followed. Shi Lan read it without changing her expression. The marked place was already outside the proposed burn, part of the manually cleared deep-soil strip. Whoever wrote the warning had either misunderstood the map or meant something else. Lin looked toward the cold hollow. A warning could be useful even if its method was foolish. The removed flag had still made the crew's boundary harder to see.

forest_07_045.speaker: shi_lan
forest_07_045.text: Replace the flag and stop this edge while we ask the gathering households what the writer may have seen. I want the note posted as an offered warning, with its original kept in the office. No one will be punished for bringing an observation. Cutting a line flag is different; I will ask that person to explain it. If we frighten every worried neighbor into silence, the next warning may arrive only after smoke does.

forest_07_046.speaker: narrator
forest_07_046.text: By noon, an elderly gatherer admitted moving the flag. She had watched a planning visitor point toward her late husband's favorite resting tree and feared it would be burned. She could not read the map well enough to identify the exclusion. Her grandson had written the note. Shi Lan walked the edge with her and showed the protected tree. The woman touched its bark, embarrassed by the attention. The warden asked her to use the watch station next time instead of hiding the flag.

forest_07_047.speaker: narrator
forest_07_047.text: The visitor had been Long's manager, discussing access rather than the burn edge. He came to explain his gesture and apologized for pointing broadly where people were trying to read a precise plan. The gatherer listened, then asked him to carry her small bundle to the gate since he was walking that way. He accepted. Wen watched them leave together and said some misunderstandings had surprisingly practical endings. The senior worker told him not to start hiding flags to improve carriage service.

forest_07_048.speaker: narrator
forest_07_048.text: The flag incident reached the town through a badly summarized message. Before the correction arrived, Rong's office received a report of deliberate interference with the burn line. His brother wrote asking whether local opponents were sabotaging supply. Rong brought the letter to Pei instead of answering from rumor. The old keeper sighed so deeply that Lin expected the desk to settle. She dictated the actual sequence and requested that future messages distinguish an incident from the sender's theory about it.

forest_07_049.speaker: narrator
forest_07_049.text: Rong read the correction while Lin held the copied flag note beneath its date. He said his brother disliked uncertainty because the office had once lost a winter shipment to a false assurance. Pei said that history should make him more careful, not more certain. Rong answered that fear rarely chose the most elegant lesson. Lin thought of the clerk's flour explanation and kept quiet. Rong signed the corrected message and sent it before writing anything about sabotage.

forest_07_050.speaker: rong_sui
forest_07_050.text: I can tell my brother there is no evidence of sabotage here. I cannot tell him every future warning will be harmless. That difference will annoy him. He will write back with three questions and a proposal that sounds efficient from town. If you see me repeating it without checking the hillside, remind me of the folded flag. I do not require gentleness. I may require a second reminder after I finish explaining why this time is different.

forest_07_051.speaker: narrator
forest_07_051.text: The crew finished the revised manual strip over the following two days. No one had lit it. The dark seam remained damp and excluded. Lin's palms hardened at the spots the shovel touched most often; the superficial splinter cut closed cleanly under ordinary care. She could work a full assigned preparation turn with fewer wasted swings now. The improvement was in her hands and timing. Her cultivation remained fourth stage, still requiring its separate measured practice when she had rested enough for it.

forest_07_052.speaker: narrator
forest_07_052.text: Wen's knee passed its next clinic review, and he returned gradually to the slope tasks. He celebrated by carrying a bundle slightly smaller than he would have chosen a month earlier. Lin noticed but did not praise him aloud. He noticed her noticing and said she could applaud after the bundle reached its stack. At the stack, she clapped once. The senior worker asked whether this was a new system of labor encouragement. Wen said it was highly selective and badly funded.

forest_07_053.speaker: narrator
forest_07_053.text: On the third afternoon, the district wildlife investigator called at the dealer's lodging. The purchase register showed ordinary shed antlers from two licensed sources, but no record of the intact-pair premium advertised here. The dealer blamed the printer again. His actual order book contained a town customer's request for fresh matched pairs. He admitted that request had influenced the notice. He denied arranging traps. The investigator suspended the questionable purchase offer while examining the snare and local accounts.

forest_07_054.speaker: narrator
forest_07_054.text: The dealer's wagon could leave with its ordinary documented goods after inspection, but the district office retained certified copies of the relevant order and register. The dealer wanted his posting payment refunded. The poster refused, saying he had done the work. The argument spilled into the square, where people heard enough to create five different stories. Lin carried the public inquiry notice to the watch station. She repeated only the actual restriction and the request for information about traps.

forest_07_055.speaker: narrator
forest_07_055.text: At the watch station, a boy admitted seeing a man kneel beside the low track before the first Hart appeared. He had been collecting pinecones with his grandmother. He could describe a grey cap and a red cart strap, not a face. Several local workers owned both. Shi Lan invited the grandmother's separate account rather than make the boy repeat his description until it became sharper than his memory. He looked disappointed that he had not solved the whole mystery.

forest_07_056.speaker: narrator
forest_07_056.text: The grandmother remembered the man carrying something long under his coat. It might have been a tool. She had kept the child away because strangers at the low track made her wary. She could place the visit after the last market day and before the cabbage damage. The investigator wrote the interval, not a guessed hour. Lin had begun to find patience less noble and more muscular: it meant holding a question open while every person nearby wanted it closed.

forest_07_057.speaker: narrator
forest_07_057.text: That evening, Long came to the lower shelter with his smaller-margin credit proposal. He had reduced the service charge for a bounded group of households affected by the new grain price, using his business margin rather than the relief stock. The terms still required repayment from named paid work, with review for employer default. A woman asked whether the proposal would last after he stopped feeling watched. He gave its expiry date and the renewal condition. She said that was the answer she had wanted.

forest_07_058.speaker: narrator
forest_07_058.text: Lin helped the clerk read the proposed terms to people who requested it. She stayed clear of advising them which debt to choose. One man decided to buy less grain for cash instead. Another accepted the credit after his partner read the repayment schedule. The woman who had questioned Long returned with her work slips and asked two more precise questions. The clerk answered both without looking toward the buyer for permission. Long watched from the door, learning how little his presence needed to dominate.

forest_07_059.speaker: narrator
forest_07_059.text: Near closing, a young carrier accused Long of making profit from a broken road. Long said the extra carriage had cost more than the announced increase would recover this month. The carrier asked to see the public price explanation. Long produced it. The carrier read, frowned, and said the explanation did not make him richer. Long agreed. For a moment the two men had no argument left except the poverty neither could politely summarize. Then the carrier asked about next week's hiring turns.

forest_07_060.speaker: narrator
forest_07_060.text: Rong arrived during that conversation and waited outside rather than interrupt it. He had brought a town proposal for advancing money against the later six-bag reserve release. The proposal would help immediate cash flow but require repayment if the reserve was used for losses instead. Long read it and shook his head. The reserve existed because losses were possible. Turning it into secured income would sell the uncertainty they had just agreed to keep visible. Rong looked relieved that someone else had rejected it first.

forest_07_061.speaker: rong_sui
forest_07_061.text: My brother calls it a bridge until the weather settles. I can see the attraction. A bridge should have somewhere firm at both ends. Here one end is six bags we may need because the weather does not settle. I will decline the advance on these terms. If he asks what we will do for money instead, I will have to give him a less comfortable answer. That is probably why I brought the page here before deciding.

forest_07_062.speaker: narrator
forest_07_062.text: Lin walked home with Wen after the office closed. He asked whether businesspeople ever slept without a number behind their eyes. She said Rong had carried the paper boat for two days without converting it into freight. Wen said that might be the beginning of recovery. At his sister's house, the good door had a new scratch from a moved stool. She had noticed and chosen not to sand it immediately. A house being used was already different from a house being wished for.

forest_07_063.speaker: narrator
forest_07_063.text: In the lodging, Shi Lan unfolded the current fire map beside the old scar in her sleeve. The prepared line now met the design after its changes. The next step was a qualified operational review, with weather observations, crew coverage, water, tools, routes, and the off-site effects considered together. Lin took the kettle to fill it before it froze again. The niece followed, asking whether a wise kettle could predict rain. Lin said it could predict tea, if adults remembered to bring water.

forest_07_064.speaker: narrator
forest_07_064.text: The operational reviewer came with a coat so stiff from old rain that it creaked when he sat. He had worked with Shi Lan before and greeted the senior worker's kettle first. The warden said the kettle was becoming insufferable. The reviewer spread the current map, the soil exclusions, and the preparation record across a long bench. He asked the crew to walk the actual line before discussing an ignition date. The map could wait while the ground introduced itself.

forest_07_065.speaker: narrator
forest_07_065.text: They walked in cold sunshine. The reviewer examined the deep-soil seam, the cleared mineral strip, the dead-tree work, and the refuge corridor. At the upper corner he found a hanging branch that the saw crew had marked for removal but had not yet taken down. He kept that section outside operational approval until the task was complete. Long's manager, attending again, wrote the remaining condition without sighing. Lin suspected repeated walks had begun to make him respect branches more than timetables.

forest_07_066.speaker: narrator
forest_07_066.text: At the refuge boundary, the reviewer asked where smoke might travel if the wind changed within the forecast range. Shi Lan showed the shelter and gathering routes. The protected hollow could trap smoke under a low inversion, even if flames stayed inside the patch. The current plan needed an additional local observation before any burn. Wen looked into the white hollow. Its cold had seemed like shelter from fire. Now he could imagine air lying there too still to clear.

forest_07_067.speaker: shi_lan
forest_07_067.text: We will add the hollow observation and the smoke trigger. If smoke begins settling on the occupied route, ignition stops and the qualified crew follows the suppression plan. The watch will keep people out of that turn before we begin. I want the alternative gathering hours posted early, with the carrier arrangements checked. Nobody should learn the plan by arriving with a child and finding a line of men holding tools across the path.

forest_07_068.speaker: narrator
forest_07_068.text: The crew checked water access at the upper tank and the lower spring. The upper tank's draw valve leaked when opened fully. A maintenance worker replaced its worn packing and tested the accepted flow. The repair consumed part of the already authorized equipment allowance. Lin carried the old packing to the tool shed, where the senior worker threw it into the rejected-parts box. He said the box was his most reliable collection of lessons because none could be reused accidentally.

forest_07_069.speaker: narrator
forest_07_069.text: Wen asked how much water the plan needed. The reviewer pointed him to the actual operational calculation and reserve margin, checked against the available tanks and replenishment. He did not give an inspiring answer about courage. Wen read the figures, then went to verify the lower path remained passable for the refill cart. The path was passable but crowded by two misplaced wood stacks. Their owners moved the stacks after the council explained the needed clearance and assigned paid handling help.

forest_07_070.speaker: narrator
forest_07_070.text: The hanging branch came down the following morning under the saw crew's controlled work. The reviewer returned to inspect that condition and the revised smoke plan. He approved readiness for a limited burn only within the stated ground and weather conditions, with named qualified leaders and a fully funded crew. No one had authority to substitute a convenient date for those conditions. Shi Lan put the approval in the office. The niece asked whether this meant her aunt could come to the next visiting meal on time.

forest_07_071.speaker: narrator
forest_07_071.text: Shi Lan checked her roster and said she could attend if the possible operation did not occur that afternoon; another caregiver's accepted turn covered the alternative. The child said fires always got the first invitation. The warden tried to explain, saw the child's face, and stopped. She knelt to promise an ordinary supper together the next night. That promise was small enough to keep. Lin watched her mark it on the same page as the work roster.

forest_07_072.speaker: narrator
forest_07_072.text: Before the possible window, the council renewed the funded preparation and observation interval after its scheduled review. Operational wages, relief coverage, and the qualified crew's callout were separately approved within the reviewed amount. Delays would require later review rather than silent extensions. The injured shoulder worker remained off lifting; his immediate food portion and medical follow-up were arranged. He sent a message wishing the crew a boring fire. The senior worker called it the highest professional blessing available.

forest_07_073.speaker: narrator
forest_07_073.text: Rong received his brother's rejection of the declined reserve advance. The letter accused him of losing commercial nerve. He read it twice, then went outside to pace. Lin met him by the well and nearly retreated from the expression on his face. He asked whether she had ever been called timid for refusing a reckless task. She said yes. He said he had expected the accusation to become less effective with age. It had acquired better handwriting, not less force.

forest_07_074.speaker: rong_sui
forest_07_074.text: He is younger than I am. He learned accounts from me. Now he writes as though my hesitation has become the obstacle between our office and success. I can answer every point and still hear him saying I am afraid. I am afraid. I am afraid of another customer freezing, another crew borrowing flour, another false report arriving with my name above it. The question is what the fear makes me buy. Today it will not buy those six uncertain bags.

forest_07_075.speaker: narrator
forest_07_075.text: He returned to the office and wrote a firm answer. Lin left him there. She went to the practice mat after eating, where the small controlled fourth-stage sequence required less interpretation than her day. The first return blurred when she thought about Rong's letter. She released, rested, and began again within her usual measured allowance. The second sequence held. She did not mistake calm hands for a complete answer to the forest. They were simply useful hands.

forest_07_076.speaker: narrator
forest_07_076.text: At supper, Shi Lan kept the promised ordinary meal with her niece. The girl made her aunt sit in the chair nearest the warm wall and served her a potato with great ceremony. Wen declared himself deputy inspector of whether the potato was eaten. Shi Lan said the commission had enough deputies. Lin watched the warden finish the potato before checking any map. The child looked pleased in a way that required no applause.

forest_07_077.speaker: narrator
forest_07_077.text: Later, the senior fireline worker told Lin that the man injured nine years earlier lived in the next valley and mended tools now. Shi Lan visited him whenever the route and his invitation allowed. Their friendship had survived, though he could still make her wince by recalling the retrieved tool. It had been a cheap iron scraper. Lin looked at the keeper's rejected-parts box and understood why some ordinary objects grew larger in a memory than they ever were in a hand.

forest_07_078.speaker: narrator
forest_07_078.text: On the last preparation evening, Wen sat beside Lin at the western shelter while the observation crew finished its readings. The possible burn window was approaching, and the air smelled of dry needles above wet earth. He asked whether she trusted Shi Lan. Lin said yes, including her ability to cancel. Wen considered that. He said canceling would disappoint people who had already changed their work hours. Lin said beginning wrongly could disappoint them with a fire instead.

forest_07_079.speaker: wen_cai
forest_07_079.text: I know. I am not arguing for a wrong fire. I am trying to understand why doing the right thing can still make everybody glare at the person who does it. My uncle says the warden enjoys saying no because it keeps her important. I told him that was unfair. Then I imagined myself waiting here all week for the paid operation turn and heard how tempting the unfair sentence becomes. I would like to earn the wage. That is true too.

forest_07_080.speaker: narrator
forest_07_080.text: Lin admitted she wanted the work to proceed partly because she had spent so many days clearing the line. Wen looked relieved by the admission. They sat without polishing either wish. Above them, the observation ribbon moved weakly east while the smoke from the shelter flue sank along the shaded shelf. The senior worker noticed the difference and wrote it down. The air had begun offering a reason to wait before anyone had decided whether waiting was bearable.

forest_07_081.speaker: narrator
forest_07_081.text: At the office, Pei placed the current forecast beside the actual local readings. The possible front had slowed, leaving cold still air over the hollow longer than expected. The morning decision would use both sources. Long's manager asked whether the council could at least announce likely ignition. Shi Lan said likely was already in the notice; no new certainty had arrived. The manager copied the reply and left, his face suggesting he would rather carry fir branches again.

forest_07_082.speaker: narrator
forest_07_082.text: Lin helped set the morning meeting table, then went home by the good-door house. Wen's sister was oiling the hinges. She said a new door deserved a little care before winter tried to teach it manners. Inside, the intended husband had fallen asleep with a peg bag on his lap. Lin laughed softly. The sister asked whether the burn would happen. Lin said the warden would decide after the readings. The sister nodded and returned to the hinge without demanding a prettier answer.

forest_07_083.speaker: narrator
forest_07_083.text: The night stayed clear. In the cold hollow, vapor rose from black water and lay low beneath the branches. On the sunny ridge, the cleared line showed pale against dark litter. Two neighboring slopes held different conditions under the same stars. Shi Lan stood outside the lodging for a long time before returning to bed. Lin heard her steps, then the careful quiet of a woman trying not to wake a child who had finally gone to sleep.

forest_07_084.speaker: narrator
forest_07_084.text: Before dawn, the senior worker's kettle remained liquid under its insulated cover. This small victory improved everyone's mood until the observation runner arrived. The hollow was still holding smoke from the distant morning stoves, and the wind above the patch had begun shifting unevenly. Shi Lan took the readings, put down her tea, and called the qualified leaders to the office. The prepared line was ready. The morning was not yet answering the same question.
